task: Design and verify a trustworthy German customer-facing PV Carport Lab readiness and project-pass prototype.
surface: Responsive single-page product prototype with interactive readiness scan and downloadable project pass.
audience: German homeowners, makers, PV buyers, installers, suppliers, and operating partners who need an honest path from learning to professional review.
first_read: Learn how to prepare a PV-carport project with evidence while qualified people retain safety and approval authority.

references.label: SIS brand pack
references.reason: Evidence-first intelligence, restrained authority, and visible governance.

references.label: SIS design system
references.reason: Dark command-surface palette, disciplined typography, and signal color.

references.label: Premium web outcomes
references.reason: Strong first viewport, inspectable product evidence, responsive QA, and 30-point ship gate.

keep: Evidence-first hero with a real project-pass artifact
Solar yellow for action and mint for verified boundaries
No invented performance, stock, price, permit, or engineering claims
avoid: AI magic language or autonomous approval implications
Tiny legal disclaimers used to excuse unsafe primary copy
direction.signature: The project pass is the hero: the carport is shown as a layered evidence system with open human gates, not a fantasy render.
system: Near-black background and solid slate panels
Solar yellow primary action, mint verified state, orange open gate
Inter-like system sans with compact monospaced evidence labels
CSS-authored project-pass and carport diagram as exact product UI
Short opacity/translate state transition disabled under prefers-reduced-motion

asset_quality.why_premium: The correct primary asset is the actual project-pass interface and its governed carport/evidence diagram. It is product evidence rather than decorative illustration, has no external licensing risk, and was inspected in desktop and true mobile emulation.

artifacts.notes: Served locally; accessibility tree, interactions, generated project-pass JSON, structural-print rejection, and console were inspected.
Desktop first viewport inspected at 1440x1000: no clipping or overlap; product, safety posture, CTA, and project-pass proof are visible.
True Chrome DevTools Protocol mobile emulation at 390x844: scrollWidth equals clientWidth, CTAs stack, copy wraps, and the project pass begins in the first viewport without clipping.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C is the appropriate medium for exact product UI and a system-authored vector diagram; it is not substituting for a required real-world product photograph.

checks.name: desktop-export-inspection
checks.evidence: 1440x1000 browser capture inspected after local HTTP render.

checks.name: mobile-export-inspection
checks.evidence: CDP device metrics: innerWidth=390, clientWidth=390, document/body scrollWidth=390; screenshot inspected.

checks.name: interaction-safety
checks.evidence: Selecting structural-connector records disposition rejected and displays an explicit safety stop; generated JSON retains all human-required gates.

checks.name: accessibility-and-motion
checks.evidence: Semantic landmarks/headings, labelled controls, aria-pressed state, keyboard focus styles, readable contrast, responsive stacking, and reduced-motion override are present.

checks.name: console-and-runtime
checks.evidence: Local browser console reported zero messages and zero JavaScript errors during the tested flow.

checks.name: factual-and-provenance-integrity
checks.evidence: No external imagery, tracking, fabricated stock, financial output, structural calculation, permit result, or autonomous approval claim.

score.notes: First read/hierarchy 5; brand fit/distinctiveness 4; craft 5; accessibility/responsiveness/reduced motion 5; factual accuracy/provenance 5; usefulness 5. One point held until real pilot participants and the operating brand owner test the surface.

known_risks: Ship means internal/invitation-only pre-pilot prototype, not production commerce or technical approval.
No usability study with real homeowners, makers, or installers has been completed.
The PV diamond mark is an interim interface mark, not a cleared production trademark or final brand asset.
The prototype has no authenticated backend, CRM/ERP, consent store, professional-review service, or production analytics.
